title: Pizza Box Diagonal
preview: An 18-inch round pizza needs to fit in a square box. Will it? Use the Pythagorean theorem to compare the diagonal to the pizza diameter.

body.goal: Apply the Pythagorean theorem to find the diagonal of a square in a real-world packaging context, and compare exact values to make a decision.
body.studentPrompt:
A pizzeria sells round pizzas in square boxes. Three box sizes are in the supply room:

| Box | Inside dimensions (in) |
|---|---|
| Small | 12 × 12 |
| Medium | 14 × 14 |
| Large | 16 × 16 |

A round pizza fits in a square box only if the pizza's **diameter** is ≤ the **inside side length** of the box.

1. Compute each box's **diagonal** to the nearest tenth of an inch.
2. An **18-inch (diameter) round pizza** needs to be stored. Does it fit in any of the boxes? Explain.
3. A pizza is folded in half (a half-circle). The half-circle's straight edge is 18 inches. Could it fit *diagonally* in one of the boxes? Compare 18 to each box's diagonal.
4. **Reverse it.** What's the smallest square box (whole inches per side) that fits an 18-inch pizza?
5. The pizzeria wants every box's diagonal to be at least 18 inches (so any pizza folded once will fit diagonally). What minimum **side length** does that require? Round up to the nearest whole inch.
6. A circular pizza of diameter d fits inside a square box of side s only if d ≤ s (not d ≤ diagonal). Why? Sketch the situation.

image.alt: A cardboard delivery pizza box on a white windowsill in daylight.

body.launch: Don't pre-teach diagonal formula. Hand out the box sizes. Send groups to the boards. Q3 forces the diagonal-vs-side distinction.
body.btcFit: Q6 is the diamond — students might naively think a round pizza can fit if its diameter equals the box's diagonal. But a circle inscribed in a square has diameter = side, not diagonal.
body.anticipatedApproaches:
- Q1: 12-12 box: √(12² + 12²) = √288 ≈ 17.0. 14-14: √392 ≈ 19.8. 16-16: √512 ≈ 22.6.
- Q2: An 18-inch pizza needs side ≥ 18. None of the three boxes work (largest is 16).
- Q3: 18 vs diagonals: 17.0 (small no), 19.8 (medium yes), 22.6 (large yes). The folded pizza fits diagonally in the medium and large boxes.
- Q4: Smallest box with side ≥ 18 → **18 × 18**.
- Q5: Need diagonal ≥ 18 → s√2 ≥ 18 → s ≥ 18/√2 ≈ 12.73. Round up to **13 inches**.
- Q6: A round pizza inscribed in a square fits when its diameter equals the box's side. The diagonal is √2 times longer than the side — but the round pizza only uses one side direction at a time. So d ≤ s, not d ≤ diagonal.
body.commonMisconceptions:
- Computing the diagonal as 2·side (no — that's the perimeter of a half-square, not the diagonal).
- For Q2, comparing 18 to the diagonal of the small box (17) and saying 'almost fits.'
- For Q5, dividing 18 by 2 instead of √2 (gets 9 — too small).
- For Q6, claiming a round pizza fits if its diameter ≤ box diagonal (intuition fails — the round pizza needs the FULL side, not the diagonal).
body.discussionQuestions:
- Why does a folded (half-circle) pizza fit diagonally when the round version doesn't?
- The diagonal of an n × n square is n√2. Why √2? Where does that come from?
- A 'square' pizza (cut from a circular one, kept square) fits in a smaller box than a round pizza. Why?
- The medium box has diagonal 19.8 — bigger than 18. But the round 18-inch pizza still won't fit. Why?
body.extensions:
- A rectangular box is 15 × 12 inches. What's its diagonal? Does the round 18-inch pizza fit?
- The pizzeria considers a hexagonal box. The distance across (flat-to-flat) is 18 in. What's the across-corners distance? Does an 18-inch round pizza fit corner-to-corner?
- A pizza is sliced into a rectangle 15 × 10 inches. What's the smallest *square* box that holds it (without folding)?
- Sketch how a round pizza of diameter d fits in a square box of side d. Compare to a folded version.
body.sampleSolutions:
1. Small: √(12² + 12²) = √288 ≈ **17.0 in**. Medium: √392 ≈ **19.8 in**. Large: √512 ≈ **22.6 in**.
2. An 18-in round pizza needs side ≥ 18. **None of the three boxes work**.
3. 18 vs diagonals: 17 (no), 19.8 (yes), 22.6 (yes). Folded pizza fits diagonally in medium and large.
4. **18 × 18 box** (smallest whole side ≥ 18).
5. s√2 ≥ 18 → s ≥ 12.73 → **13 inches** (whole inches, round up).
6. A round pizza needs the full diameter in each direction. The diagonal is only used by the folded half-circle. So d ≤ s.
